title: Add end-to-end token-path timing map and runbook-linked log rollups
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new end-to-end token-path timing map, sampled log-rollups tied to runs, and an on-call runbook for noisy token-latency incidents. Improvements should reduce noisy pages and make SLO RCA faster.
description:
Context and motivation: Customer incident postmortem (ENG-9119) highlighted that long-tail token latency often originates from multi-stage amplification (gateway queueing -> kernel stalls -> KV-cache misses) but lacked an easy way to trace per-token timing across the entire pipeline. This PR introduces an end-to-end token-path timing map plus a lightweight sampled log-rollup that links a condensed runbook snippet to top anomalies so on-call can TTR faster.

What this changes (high level): 1) Telemetry: new per-invocation token-path histogram that records micro-phase timings (ingest->queue->dispatch->exec->kv-lookup->streaming) with labeled buckets; supports aggregation by route/model/tenant. 2) Trace enrichment: span metadata now includes a compact token-path fingerprint (sha1) so related spans can be grouped even when trace ids differ (cross-service handoffs). 3) Rollups: sampled log-rollups emit compact log digests for high-cost invocations and attach a runbook reference id for automated incident hints. 4) Alert tuning: updated alert rule to use token-path SLO percentiles and dynamic noise attenuation to suppress low-impact pages. 5) Console/Dashboard: added a Token Path Timing Map dashboard with heatmap and top fingerprint list. 6) Test/bench: synthetic replay test and microbench to validate histogram accuracy and sampling determinism.

Commits summary: - Add token_path_timer histogram proto, serializer, and storage adapter - Emit token_path fingerprint as span tag during pipeline handoff - Implement sampled_log_rollup actor and compact digest format - Dashboard: token-path timing map panels and fingerprint explorer - Runbook: short-runbook snippets and link resolver for runbook ids - Tests: deterministic sampling unit tests + replaybench to assert percentiles

Files changed (high level): - telemetry/metrics/token_path_timer.proto (new) - runtime/invocation/path_profiler.rs (new) - tracing/span_enricher.go (add fingerprint tag) - observability/rollups/sampled_log_rollup.py (new) - dashboards/token_path_timing_map.json (new dashboard) - docs/runbooks/token_latency_quickstart.md (new runbook) - tests/replaybench/token_path_bench.py (new) - ci/workflows/telemetry.yml (updated to include replaybench) - observability/alerts/token_path_slo.rule (updated) - pkg/telemetry/README.md (docs)

Review conversation (condensed and chronological): - Liam: "Nice end-to-end here — can we make the fingerprint stable across restarts?" Author: "Fingerprint uses model+route+sha1(prefixes)+seed; added deterministic seed based on invocation id to address this." - Maya: "The sampled rollup format looks good, but worried about cardinality in the fingerprint index." Author: "We cap the fingerprint index to top-N per minute and use reservoir sampling for rollups; added metrics to monitor index growth." - Carlos: "Alert changes look likely to reduce noise, can we add a fast-toggle flag if we need to revert during incidents?" Author: "Added feature flag telemetry.token_path_soft_quiet_mode and a console toggle; documented revert steps in runbook." - CI: initial run failed (replaybench mismatch on percentile under high concurrency). Author fixed kernel scheduling race in path_profiler and resubmitted; CI green on rerun. - Final approvals: Liam (approved), Maya (approved), Carlos (approved).

CI and validation: - Unit tests: all pass. - Replaybench: deterministic pass with three different seed scenarios. - Integration smoke: deployed to canary (dedicated namespace) for 48h; observed 12% reduction in pages for the noisy tenant in synthetic test. - Load test: <5% p95 overhead on happy-path requests when token_path_timer is enabled in sampling mode.

Operational notes & runbook pointers: - New metric names: telemetry.token_path_timer.* and telemetry.token_path_fingerprint.count - Rollup export stored in s3://redwood-observability/rollups/{date}/fingerprint={fp} - Runbook quickstart located at docs/runbooks/token_latency_quickstart.md; includes steps to flip token_path_soft_quiet_mode and how to query top fingerprints. - Emergency revert: revert feature flag via console -> feature toggles -> telemetry.token_path_soft_quiet_mode = off; if needed, rollback edge/ingest change with rollback job telemetry/rollback/token-path-rollback.yaml

Migration and rollout plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable sampling only for 2 test tenants for 48h (already done). - Phase 2 (staged): progressive enablement by customer size over 7 days with monitoring dashboards. - Phase 3 (global): enable default sampling and rollup indexing for all tenants; feature flagged so we can soft-quiet at runtime.

Why this is unique: Instead of only attributing cost/latency to broad stages, the token-path timing map stitches per-token micro-phase timings into a compact fingerprint that surfaces recurring cross-service amplification patterns. Pairing compact sampled log-rollups and a runbook link dramatically reduces investigation time for noisy tail events.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - Add optional kv-cache occupancy metric to path_profiler (ENG-9199) - Wire runbook snippets to PagerDuty incident templates - Long-term: index fingerprint similarities to suggest causal clusters (future PR)

Merge outcome: Squash merged on main (2025-02-22) after approvals and CI green.

Notes for reviewers: This PR touches both runtime and observability paths; changes are feature flagged and safe to revert. If you're reviewing the rollup serializer, focus on compactness and forward-compatibility (we include a version byte).
